config.title: useWindowSize

intro.title: useWindowSize
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom Angular hook called `useWindowSize` that tracks the current width and height of the browser window. You will learn how to use the `window` object to listen for resize events and update component state accordingly. The main technologies involved are Angular's `OnInit` and `OnDestroy` lifecycle hooks, RxJS for handling events, and TypeScript for type safety. By the end, you'll have a reusable hook that dynamically responds to window size changes, enhancing your understanding of reactive state management in Angular.
intro.usecase: The useWindowSize pattern is essential for creating responsive interfaces that adapt to different screen sizes in real-time. In dashboard applications, developers use window size detection to rearrange charts, tables, and widgets when users resize their browser or switch between desktop and tablet modes. E-commerce sites implement this to adjust product grids, navigation menus, and image galleries dynamically. Media players and data visualization tools rely on window size tracking to optimize layout and maintain usability across devices, ensuring content remains accessible and visually balanced regardless of viewport changes.

objectives: Implement a custom Angular service to track browser window dimensions
Initialize reactive state variables for window width and height
Configure event listeners for window resize events
Bind window dimensions to component templates using Angular's data binding
Manipulate component layout based on dynamic window size changes
Integrate the window size service across multiple Angular components
Control component visibility or styling through window size conditions

steps.title: Import Component, OnInit, HostListener, and Injectable from Angular core
steps.instruction: Import Component, OnInit, HostListener, and Injectable from '@angular/core'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to bring in multiple symbols from the Angular core module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple Angular core features
import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core';
steps.seedCode: // Import Component, OnInit, HostListener, and Injectable from '@angular/core'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Angular core imports needed for window size tracking are added to the file.
successCriteria: Component, OnInit, HostListener, and Injectable are imported from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but not all required imports are present. Make sure to import Component, OnInit, HostListener, and Injectable from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The required imports are missing. Please import Component, OnInit, HostListener, and Injectable from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Create a WindowSizeService with window size state
steps.instruction: Create a new Angular service class named WindowSizeService that includes width and height properties to track the window dimensions.
steps.hint: Use the @Injectable() decorator and define two public properties, width and height, initialized with default values (e.g., 0).
steps.expectedOutcome: The WindowSizeService class is defined with public width and height properties.
successCriteria: WindowSizeService is an @Injectable() class with public width and height properties (both numbers).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the service, but make sure both width and height properties are present and public.
steps.feedbackWrong: The service is missing or incorrectly defined. Ensure you have an @Injectable() class named WindowSizeService with width and height properties.

steps.title: Initialize window size state in the service constructor
steps.instruction: In the WindowSizeService constructor, set initial values for the width and height properties using window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight.
steps.hint: Access the global window object directly. Assign window.innerWidth to this.width and window.innerHeight to this.height inside the constructor.
steps.expectedOutcome: The service constructor now sets initial window dimensions when the service is instantiated.
successCriteria: The constructor assigns window.innerWidth to a width property and window.innerHeight to a height property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're assigning both width and height properties using window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight.
steps.feedbackWrong: The constructor should set initial width and height values using window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight.

steps.title: Add HostListener to track window resize events
steps.instruction: In the WindowSizeService, add a method decorated with @HostListener that listens to the 'window:resize' event and updates the width and height properties.
steps.hint: Use the @HostListener decorator above a method that takes an event parameter. Inside the method, update this.width and this.height with window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight.
steps.expectedOutcome: The service now has a method that automatically updates window dimensions when the browser window is resized.
successCriteria: A method decorated with @HostListener('window:resize', ['$event']) is added to the service, and it updates this.width and this.height with window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your method has the @HostListener decorator with the correct event and updates both width and height properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HostListener method is missing or incomplete. Check that you've added the decorator and implemented the resize logic correctly.

steps.title: Create a WindowSizeComponent that uses the service
steps.instruction: Create a new component class named WindowSizeComponent that injects the WindowSizeService in its constructor.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator to define the component and add a constructor parameter with the service type.
steps.expectedOutcome: A WindowSizeComponent class is created with the WindowSizeService injected in its constructor.
successCriteria: The WindowSizeComponent class exists with @Component decorator and a constructor that injects WindowSizeService.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've created the WindowSizeComponent class with @Component decorator and injected the service in the constructor.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you have the @Component decorator and constructor with WindowSizeService parameter.

steps.title: Implement OnInit in the component
steps.instruction: In the WindowSizeComponent class, implement the OnInit interface and add an ngOnInit method.
steps.hint: Add 'implements OnInit' after the class name and define ngOnInit() {} inside the class body.
steps.expectedOutcome: The WindowSizeComponent class now implements OnInit and has an empty ngOnInit method ready for initialization logic.
successCriteria: WindowSizeComponent implements OnInit interface and contains an ngOnInit method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure both the 'implements OnInit' is added after the class name AND the ngOnInit() method is defined inside the class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't properly implement OnInit. Check that you've added 'implements OnInit' after the class name and defined ngOnInit() {} inside the class body.

steps.title: Access window size data from the service
steps.instruction: In the WindowSizeComponent, add two public properties named 'width' and 'height' that reference the corresponding values from the injected WindowSizeService.
steps.hint: You'll need to inject the service in the component's constructor and assign its width and height properties to your component's properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have width and height properties that hold the current window dimensions from the service.
successCriteria: The WindowSizeComponent has width and height properties that are assigned values from the WindowSizeService.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both width and height properties are properly assigned from the service.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't yet have the required properties accessing the service data. Try adding width and height properties that reference the service values.

steps.title: Create the component template structure
steps.instruction: Add a basic template structure inside the component's template property with placeholders for displaying the window width and height values.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to bind the component's width and height properties in the template.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: template structure with bound values template: '

Width: {{ width }}

Height: {{ height }}

'
steps.expectedOutcome: The component's template property will contain HTML structure with placeholders for width and height values using Angular's interpolation syntax.
successCriteria: The template property contains at least one HTML element with {{ width }} and {{ height }} interpolation bindings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some template structure, but make sure to include both width and height placeholders using interpolation syntax {{ }}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure doesn't appear to have the required placeholders. Try adding HTML elements with {{ width }} and {{ height }} bindings.

steps.title: Display current window width and height
steps.instruction: In the WindowSizeComponent template, use interpolation to display the current width and height values from the component's properties.
steps.hint: Angular interpolation uses double curly braces {{ }} to bind component properties to the template. For example: {{ width }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show the current window dimensions when the component renders.
successCriteria: The template contains interpolation expressions {{ width }} and {{ height }} that display the component's width and height properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using interpolation syntax {{ }} with the correct property names.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet display the width and height values. Remember to use interpolation with double curly braces.

steps.title: Add responsive styling to visualize changes
steps.instruction: In the WindowSizeComponent's template, add a div with inline styles that change based on the current window dimensions. Use the width and height from the service to set the div's background color and dimensions.
steps.hint: You can use Angular's style binding syntax like [style.width.px]="width" and [style.background-color]="width > 768 ? 'lightblue' : 'lightcoral'". Make sure to access the width and height properties you defined earlier.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: responsive div with inline styles
Responsive box
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display a responsive colored box that visually changes size and color as you resize the browser window.
successCriteria: The template contains a div element with inline styles bound to the width and height properties, and the background color changes conditionally based on window width.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure the div's dimensions and background color are properly bound to the width and height properties from the service.
steps.feedbackWrong: The responsive styling wasn't added correctly. Check that you're using Angular's style binding syntax and accessing the width/height properties from the component.
